content: Just a headsup: I have just started directing an agent to create the relevant files to enable the registration of the headline results of this repository (basically, the main published theorems of the PFR papers) to Palomar. Will update on how that proceeds.

A Palomar registration setup has now been made (almost entirely AI-generated) at https://github.com/teorth/pfr/pull/286 with all the needed data for Palomar (challenge file, solution file, formalization.yaml) kept separate from the main PFR repository (but using it as imports). It also corrects some minor issues with PFR itself that the agent found along the way: @Lorenzo Luccioli 's name was reversed in CITATION.cff, and some of the WeakPFR.lean material implicitly contained sorries due to a technical issue regarding how variable declaration default values (such as by volume_tac) interact with modules. Also some very minor drifts between the published versions of the theorems and the versions stated in PFR (e.g., A + A vs. A - A formulations) are corrected via some bridge lemmas in the solution file. However, I have tried to keep edits to the core PFR Lean code to an absolute minimum.

Only the combinatorial statements of the source papers are kept in the challenge file. The entropic statements are not easy to fit into the challenge file because Shannon entropy is not yet defined in Mathlib. One could have a future Palomar registry entry (on the same repository) to address this; Palomar allows multiple results to be independently registered from the same repo.

The existing list of PFR collaborators and maintainers was used to populate the relevant metadata of formalization.yaml. Please let me know (e.g., by private DM) if you would like to be removed from this list.

I'll leave the PR unmerged for now in case there is feedback, but after a few days I plan to merge and then register with Palomar.
